solution: Put \(t=4^x>0\): \(t+\frac{4}{t}-5<0\Rightarrow t^2-5t+4<0\Rightarrow (t-1)(t-4)<0\Rightarrow 1<t<4\Rightarrow 4^0<4^x<4^1\Rightarrow 0<x<1\). Hence (D).
\(4+2\sqrt3=(\sqrt3+1)^2\) and \(4-2\sqrt3=(\sqrt3-1)^2\). So the expression \(=(\sqrt3+1)-(\sqrt3-1)=2\). Hence (B).
Let \(t=|x|\ge0\): \(t^2-5t-24=0\Rightarrow (t-8)(t+3)=0\Rightarrow t=8\) (reject \(-3\)). So \(|x|=8\Rightarrow x=\pm8\). Product \(=-64\), sum \(=0\). Hence (A).
Subtracting the equations: \((b-1)x-1-b=0\Rightarrow x=\frac{1+b}{b-1}\). Substituting into \(x^2+x+b=0\) (or using the common-root condition) gives \(b^2=3\Rightarrow |b|=\sqrt3\). Hence (C).

Sum of roots \(=\tan33^\circ+\tan12^\circ=n/m\); product \(=\tan33^\circ\tan12^\circ=k/m\). Since \(33^\circ+12^\circ=45^\circ\), \(\tan45^\circ=\frac{\tan33^\circ+\tan12^\circ}{1-\tan33^\circ\tan12^\circ}=1\Rightarrow \frac{n/m}{1-k/m}=1\Rightarrow n=m-k\Rightarrow m=n+k\). So \(\frac{2m+n+k}{m}=\frac{2m+m}{m}=3\). Hence (D).
Product of roots \(\alpha\beta=\frac{-1}{4}\Rightarrow \beta=\frac{-1}{4\alpha}\). Hence (A).
\(\alpha+\alpha^2=6\Rightarrow \alpha^2+\alpha-6=0\Rightarrow \alpha=2\) (positive) or \(-3\). For \(\alpha=2\): \(c=\alpha\cdot\alpha^2=\alpha^3=8\). Hence (D).
Product of roots \(=\frac{a}{a}=1\), so the other root is \(\frac{1}{6}\). Sum \(=6+\frac{1}{6}=\frac{37}{6}=\frac{b}{a}\). Hence (C).
Equal roots: discriminant \((a+3)^2-4\cdot2\cdot8=0\Rightarrow (a+3)^2=64\Rightarrow a+3=\pm8\Rightarrow a=5\) or \(a=-11\). Hence (C).
Roots are \(p\) and \(q\). Sum: \(p+q=-p\); product: \(pq=q\). From \(pq=q\): \(q(p-1)=0\). If \(q\ne0\), \(p=1\), then \(1+q=-1\Rightarrow q=-2\). So \(p=1, q=-2\). Hence (A).

For \(>0\ \forall x\) the discriminant must be \(<0\): \(4(4k-1)^2-4(15k^2-2k-7)<0\Rightarrow (4k-1)^2-(15k^2-2k-7)<0\Rightarrow k^2-6k+8<0\Rightarrow (k-2)(k-4)<0\Rightarrow 2<k<4\Rightarrow\) integer \(k=3\) only. Exactly one. Hence (B).
\(\alpha+\beta=a,\ \alpha\beta=b^2\). \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta=a^2-2b^2\). Hence (C).
Let \(t=|x-3|\ge0\): \(t^2+t-2=0\Rightarrow (t+2)(t-1)=0\Rightarrow t=1\). So \(|x-3|=1\Rightarrow x=4\) or \(2\); sum \(=6\). Hence (C).
Replace \(x\) by \(x/3\) in \(2x^2+3x+5=0\): \(2(x/3)^2+3(x/3)+5=0\Rightarrow \frac{2x^2}{9}+x+5=0\Rightarrow 2x^2+9x+45=0\). Hence (A).

Let \(y=\frac{x}{x^2-5x+9}\Rightarrow yx^2-(5y+1)x+9y=0\). Real \(x\): \((5y+1)^2-36y^2\ge0\Rightarrow -11y^2+10y+1\ge0\Rightarrow 11y^2-10y-1\le0\Rightarrow (11y+1)(y-1)\le0\Rightarrow -\frac{1}{11}\le y\le1\). Hence (D).
Expanding: \(3x^2-2(a+b+c)x+(ab+bc+ca)=0\). Equal roots: \(4(a+b+c)^2-12(ab+bc+ca)=0\Rightarrow (a+b+c)^2=3(ab+bc+ca)\Rightarrow a^2+b^2+c^2=ab+bc+ca\). Hence (D).

\(\frac{1}{1+\sqrt3}=\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2}\). Its conjugate surd \(\frac{-\sqrt3-1}{2}\) is the other root. Sum \(=-1\), product \(=\frac{1-3}{4}=-\frac{1}{2}\). Equation: \(x^2+x-\frac{1}{2}=0\Rightarrow 2x^2+2x-1=0\). Hence (D).

Numerator \(5x^2-26x+5=(5x-1)(x-5)\), denominator \(3x^2-10x+3=(3x-1)(x-3)\). The quotient is negative on the intervals between consecutive roots \(\frac15<\frac13<3<5\): i.e. \(\frac15<x<\frac13\) or \(3<x<5\). Hence (D).

An equation with irrational coefficients cannot be forced to have two rational roots (sum/product would be rational, contradicting irrational coefficients in general); statement (C) is the one always false. Hence (C).

Roots \(\alpha,\beta\): \(\alpha+\beta=-\frac32,\ \alpha\beta=\frac12\). New roots \(\alpha^2,\beta^2\): sum \(=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta=\frac94-1=\frac54\); product \(=\frac14\). Equation \(x^2-\frac54x+\frac14=0\Rightarrow 4x^2-5x+1=0\). Hence (D).
Let \(t=3^x\): \(t^2-2\cdot9t+81=0\Rightarrow t^2-18t+81=0\Rightarrow (t-9)^2=0\Rightarrow t=9\Rightarrow 3^x=9\Rightarrow x=2\). Hence (B).
\(\alpha+\beta=-3,\ \alpha\beta=-4\). \(\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{\alpha\beta}=\frac{-3}{-4}=\frac34\). Hence (B).

\(x^2+2x+3=0\) has imaginary roots (discriminant \(<0\)). For real-coefficient \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) to share one imaginary root it must share both, so it is proportional to \(x^2+2x+3\). Thus \(a:b:c=1:2:3\). Hence (D).
\(p,q,r\) in A.P. \(\Rightarrow 2q=p+r\). \(\alpha+\beta=-q/p=4\Rightarrow q=-4p\). Then \(r=2q-p=-9p\). \(\alpha\beta=r/p=-9\). Hence (A).
Expanding gives \(3x^2-2(a+b+c)x+(ab+bc+ca)=0\), discriminant \(=4[(a+b+c)^2-3(ab+bc+ca)]=2[(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2]\). This is \(0\) iff \(a=b=c\). Hence (D).

Case \(x^2-x-6\ge0\): \(x^2-x-6=x+2\Rightarrow x^2-2x-8=0\Rightarrow x=4,-2\) (both valid). Case \(<0\): \(-(x^2-x-6)=x+2\Rightarrow x^2-4=0\Rightarrow x=\pm2\) (only \(x=2\) lies where \(x^2-x-6<0\)). Solutions \(\{4,2,-2\}\). Hence (B).

\(\alpha+\beta=-a,\ \alpha\beta=b\). New roots sum \(=(\alpha+\beta)-\frac{\alpha+\beta}{\alpha\beta}=-a(1-\frac1b)=\frac{-a(b-1)}{b}\); product \(=(\alpha-\frac1\beta)(\beta-\frac1\alpha)=\alpha\beta-2+\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}=b-2+\frac1b=\frac{(b-1)^2}{b}\). Equation \(bx^2+a(b-1)x+(b-1)^2=0\). Hence (B).
\(\alpha+\beta=a-2,\ \alpha\beta=-a-1\). \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=(a-2)^2+2(a+1)=a^2-2a+6=(a-1)^2+5\), least when \(a=1\). Hence (B).
Roots \(t,6t\): sum \(7t=\frac{14}{m}\Rightarrow t=\frac{2}{m}\); product \(6t^2=\frac{8}{m}\Rightarrow 6\cdot\frac{4}{m^2}=\frac{8}{m}\Rightarrow \frac{24}{m}=8\Rightarrow m=3\). Hence (C).

For \(x<1\), \(|x-1|=1-x\), so RHS \(\frac{x}{|x-1|}=\frac{x}{1-x}=-\frac{x}{x-1}\). Equation becomes \(\frac{x}{x-1}+|x|=-\frac{x}{x-1}\Rightarrow |x|=-\frac{2x}{x-1}\). Solving consistently gives exactly one valid real value. Hence (B).

\(\sin\theta+\cos\theta=-\frac{b}{a},\ \sin\theta\cos\theta=\frac{c}{a}\). Square the sum: \(1+2\sin\theta\cos\theta=\frac{b^2}{a^2}\Rightarrow 1+\frac{2c}{a}=\frac{b^2}{a^2}\Rightarrow a^2+2ac=b^2\Rightarrow a^2-b^2+2ac=0\). Hence (A).
Let \(t=|x|\ge0\): \(t^2-3t+2=0\Rightarrow (t-1)(t-2)=0\Rightarrow t=1,2\). Each gives two real \(x\) (\(\pm1,\pm2\)), so 4 real roots. Hence (D).
Sum of roots \(=1\). Other root \(=1-(1+i)=-i\). (Check product \((1+i)(-i)=-i-i^2=1-i\), matching the constant term.) Hence (C).
Equal roots: \((2\sqrt6)^2-4\cdot2\cdot a=0\Rightarrow 24-8a=0\Rightarrow a=3\). Hence (A).
Let \(t=|x|\ge0\): \(t^2+15t+14=0\Rightarrow (t+1)(t+14)=0\Rightarrow t=-1,-14\), both negative. No \(t\ge0\), so no real solution. Hence (C).
Roots equal and opposite \(\Rightarrow\) sum \(=0\Rightarrow \frac{a+2}{a+1}=0\Rightarrow a=-2\). Then equation \(-x^2+1=0\Rightarrow x=\pm1=\pm\frac{1}{2}a\) (since \(a=-2\)). Hence (B).
\(x^2+4ax+2>0\ \forall x\) needs discriminant \(<0\): \(16a^2-8<0\Rightarrow a^2<\frac12\Rightarrow -\frac{1}{\sqrt2}<a<\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\). Hence (D).
Real coefficients \(\Rightarrow\) roots \(2-i\) and \(2+i\). Sum \(=4=-\frac{12}{a}\Rightarrow a=-3\); product \(=5=\frac{b}{a}\Rightarrow b=-15\). \(ab=(-3)(-15)=45\). Hence (A).
Combine: \(\frac{(2x+p+q)}{(x+p)(x+q)}=\frac1r\Rightarrow x^2+(p+q-2r)x+(pq-rp-rq)=0\). Roots equal and opposite \(\Rightarrow\) sum \(=0\Rightarrow p+q-2r=0\Rightarrow p+q=2r\). Hence (B).
\(x=4\) a root of \(x^2+ax+12=0\): \(16+4a+12=0\Rightarrow a=-7\). Equal roots of \(x^2-7x+b=0\): \(49-4b=0\Rightarrow b=\frac{49}{4}\). Hence (B).
Replace \(x\) by \(x/3\) in \(3ax^2+3bx+c=0\): \(3a\frac{x^2}{9}+3b\frac{x}{3}+c=0\Rightarrow \frac{ax^2}{3}+bx+c=0\Rightarrow ax^2+3bx+3c=0\). Hence (A).
\(x^2-2ax+a^2=(x-a)^2=0\Rightarrow\) both roots \(=a\). A.M. \(=a\), G.M. \(=\sqrt{a\cdot a}=a\). So \(A=G\). Hence (A).
Roots \(\alpha,\beta\): \(\alpha+\beta=-a,\ \alpha\beta=1\). \((\alpha-\beta)^2=a^2-4<5\Rightarrow a^2<9\Rightarrow -3<a<3\). Hence (C).

\(\sec\alpha+\csc\alpha=p,\ \sec\alpha\csc\alpha=q\). Now \(\frac{1}{\sec^2\alpha}+\frac{1}{\csc^2\alpha}=\cos^2\alpha+\sin^2\alpha=1\Rightarrow \frac{\sec^2\alpha+\csc^2\alpha}{q^2}=1\). And \(\sec^2\alpha+\csc^2\alpha=p^2-2q\). So \(p^2-2q=q^2\Rightarrow p^2=q^2+2q=q(q+2)\). Hence (C).
For \(x\ge0\): \(x=x^2+x-4\Rightarrow x^2=4\Rightarrow x=2\) (reject \(-2\)). For \(x<0\): \(-x=x^2+x-4\Rightarrow x^2+2x-4=0\Rightarrow x=-1-\sqrt5\) (the negative root). Two real roots. Hence (D).
\(\frac{2^{x^2}}{2^{2x}}=2^3\Rightarrow x^2-2x=3\Rightarrow x^2-2x-3=0\Rightarrow (x-3)(x+1)=0\Rightarrow x=3,-1\). Hence (C).
Since \(|x+2|\ge 0\) for every real \(x\) while the right-hand side \(-2<0\), no value of \(x\) can satisfy \(|x+2|=-2\). Hence (C).
\(x^2-8x+(a^2-6a)=0\) real \(\Rightarrow 64-4(a^2-6a)\ge0\Rightarrow a^2-6a-16\le0\Rightarrow (a-8)(a+2)\le0\Rightarrow -2\le a\le8\). Hence (A).

\(x^2-\frac{3a}{2}x+(1-a^2)>0\ \forall x\) needs discriminant \(<0\): \(\frac{9a^2}{4}-4(1-a^2)<0\Rightarrow \frac{9a^2}{4}+4a^2<4\Rightarrow \frac{25a^2}{4}<4\Rightarrow a^2<\frac{16}{25}\Rightarrow |a|<\frac45\). Hence (D).

Complex roots occur in conjugate pairs, so \(2-3i\) is also a root. Product of all three roots \(=\frac{13}{2}\) (\(=-\frac{-13}{2}\)). \((2+3i)(2-3i)=13\), so the real root \(=\frac{13/2}{13}=\frac12\). Hence (D).

\((x^2-5x+5)^{x^2+4x-60}=1\) holds when: (i) base \(=1\): \(x^2-5x+4=0\Rightarrow x=1,4\); (ii) exponent \(=0\) (base \(\ne0\)): \(x^2+4x-60=0\Rightarrow x=-10,6\); (iii) base \(=-1\) with even exponent: \(x^2-5x+6=0\Rightarrow x=2,3\), exponent even only at \(x=2\). Valid \(x\in\{1,4,-10,6,2\}\); sum \(=3\). Hence (A).
Numerator \(x^2+6x-7=(x+7)(x-1)\); denominator \(|x+4|>0\) (\(x\ne-4\)). Inequality \(<0\Leftrightarrow (x+7)(x-1)<0\Rightarrow -7<x<1\), excluding \(x=-4\). So \((-7,-4)\cup(-4,1)\). Hence (D).

Put \(x=1,\omega,\omega^2\) (cube roots of unity) in \((1+x+x^2)^n\): at \(x=1\) value \(=3^n\); at \(x=\omega\) and \(\omega^2\), \(1+\omega+\omega^2=0\) so value \(=0\). Adding, \(3(a_0+a_3+a_6+\cdots)=3^n\Rightarrow a_0+a_3+a_6+\cdots=3^{n-1}\). Hence (A).
\(y=5x^2+2x+3=5(x+\frac15)^2+\frac{14}{5}\ge\frac{14}{5}=2.8\), while \(y=2\sin x\le2<2.8\). The curves never meet: 0 points. Hence (A).

\((1-\alpha)(1-\beta)(1-\gamma)=P(1)/(\text{leading})\) where \(P(x)=x^3-3x^2+2x-1\). \(P(1)=1-3+2-1=-1\). Since \(P(x)=(x-\alpha)(x-\beta)(x-\gamma)\), \(P(1)=(1-\alpha)(1-\beta)(1-\gamma)=-1\). Hence (C).
For \(x^3+4x+2=0\): \(\sum\alpha=0,\ \sum\alpha\beta=4,\ \alpha\beta\gamma=-2\). Each root satisfies \(\alpha^3=-4\alpha-2\), so \(\sum\alpha^3=-4\sum\alpha-6=0-6=-6\). Hence (A).
Subtract: \((b-1)x-(1+b)=0\Rightarrow x=\frac{1+b}{b-1}\). Imposing this is a common root of both leads to \(b^2=-3\) for a genuine (non-\(-1\)) common root, giving \(b=-i\sqrt3\). Hence (B).
Let \(t=|x-2|\ge0\): \(t^2+t-2=0\Rightarrow (t+2)(t-1)=0\Rightarrow t=1\). So \(|x-2|=1\Rightarrow x=3\) or \(1\); sum of real roots \(=4\). Hence (B).

Let \(t=x^4\ge0\): \(t+\sqrt{t+20}=22\Rightarrow \sqrt{t+20}=22-t\Rightarrow t+20=t^2-44t+484\Rightarrow t^2-45t+464=0\Rightarrow (t-16)(t-29)=0\). Check \(22-t\ge0\): \(t=16\) valid (\(t=29\) rejected). \(x^4=16\Rightarrow x=\pm2\): 2 real roots. Hence (B).
